prompt: Vitrine layout: responsive grid for a few hand-placed cards or tiles. Layout only; it fetches nothing and has no colours or padding of its own.
shortDesc: Responsive grid for HAND-PLACED cards only (g-artwork-card, g-collection-tile): as many columns as fit, each at least min-width wide, one column on small phones. Rarely needed: never wrap the self-loading lists (g-artwork-grid, g-collection-list, g-exhibition-list) in it, they lay themselves out. Every direct child becomes its own cell, so never put a loose g-add-to-exhibition next to a card: wrap the card and its button together in one plain <div> (the grid stacks the div's children with a small gap). Put it inside a g-page-section. Attributes: min-width="240" (px number, default 220; use ~200 for artwork cards, ~260 for collection tiles), gap="tight" | "normal" | "loose" (10 / 16 / 32px, default normal). Example: <g-grid min-width="240"><g-collection-tile collection-id="met-11" name="European Paintings" museum="The Met"></g-collection-tile></g-grid>

props.name: min-width
props.description: Minimum column width in px (default 220, clamped to 120-640; "240px" also accepted). Smaller means more columns.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between items: tight (10px), normal (16px, default) or loose (32px).

slots.description: Items to lay out; each direct child is one cell and stretches to the full row height so card captions line up. A plain <div> child stacks its own children (e.g. a card and its g-add-to-exhibition button) with a 10px gap.
slots.accepts: cards and tiles from this kit: g-artwork-card, g-collection-tile; to give a hand-picked work an add button, one <div> per cell holding <g-artwork-card> then <g-add-to-exhibition> with the same artwork-id

styling.notes: Vitrine kit. Neutral: no colours, borders or padding of its own; the surrounding g-page-section provides the band and margins, the cards provide the mats and wall labels. Gaps follow the kit spacing (10/16/32px). Collapses to a single column below 360px of available width. Direct <div> children become flex columns (10px gap) so a card and its button share one cell. Exposes part="grid".
